text:
alex: Proposal — avoid prefetch/header bias in canary splits by using a deterministic cohort seed + requiring an explicit header flag for forced overrides. current behavior: header-first match wins and we see CDNs prefetching the canary header, blowing exposure. any objections?
jess: definitely seeing this in telemetry, can confirm CDN retries labeled as canary. +1 to deterministic seed. :+1:
matt: quick sketch of a config option we could add: 
```
route {
  name: "canary-zen"
  match: [ { header: "x-redwood-canary", value: "force" } ]
  cohort_seed: "hash(tenant_id || floor(request_ts/600))"
  weight: 0.05
  header_override_mode: "explicit"  # values: explicit|prefer|ignore
}
```
priya: header_override_mode=explicit sounds right — only treat header as forcing action when value == "force" and the header came from an end-user agent (not known prefetch ASNs). we should also add a prefetch detector rule.
ana: typo — i mean ana: agree with priya. telemetry around "header_overrode_cohort" and "prefetch_origin" would help validate. we should record raw header + ip ASN so we can filter post-hoc.
console-ux: from a console POV, add a toggle in the rollout UI: "Honor client canary headers" (default off) and show an estimated additional exposure if turned on. also surface sample bias warnings if prefetch sources are high.
alex: the deterministic cohort approach prevents reassigning the same tenant to canary repeatedly across repeated prefetches, right? matt, is cohort_seed stable per-tenant?
matt: yes — seed per request window (e.g., 10m bucket) means consistent assignment for session windows; we avoid per-request noise and can still support gradual ramps by changing weight. algorithm: cohort_hash = hash(seed || tenant_id); assign if cohort_hash < (weight * MAX).
priya: edge case: what about endpoints that purposely add header for true A/B tests (client-side experiments)? we should allow an allowlist for tenants that opted into header-driven experiments.
ana: ana: +1 to tenant allowlist. also add a metric for "forced_header_assignments_by_tenant" so we can detect misuse.
eng-bot: deploy triggered: canary-config-v2 -> staging at 1729450120 by matt. link: https://deploys/redwood/canary-config-v2
jess: quick question — for rollout analytics, can we tag traces with "assignment_reason": {seed|header-forced|allowlist}
matt: yep, and we should emit both the final assignment and the decision path: e.g., "matched_header=false, header_allowed=true, cohort_assigned=true". that'll make debugging easier.
console-ux: UX note: add a small badge on the route card when header_override_mode != "ignore" to remind operators of the behavior.
ana: ana: telemetry thresholds: if >1% of canary exposure is from prefetch ASN, alert to a manual review. that threshold can be tuned.
alex: rollback plan: 1) flip header_override_mode=ignore, 2) reduce weight to 0, 3) revert cohort_seed change. which is fastest?
matt: config flip (1) is fastest and safe. config push should be <2s for control-plane-only changes.
priya: testing: let's create a smoke test that simulates prefetched requests (set x-redwood-canary force header + known prefetch ASN) and assert assignment_reason != header-forced when toggle is off.
eng-bot: staged deploy complete: canary-config-v2 -> staging at 1729450300, smoke tests: 3 passed, 1 flaky. (logs: https://ci/redwood/1729450300)
jess: nice. can we also add a small syslog entry when we detect header-but-prefetch so product can follow up with the CDN team?
alex: good convo. next steps: matt to open a PR with schema change + guardrails, priya to add ASN detector rules, console-ux to mock the toggle in staging UI, ana to add telemetry dashboards. ping me when PR is open.
priya: will do. thanks all. :smile:
